lines.intro: This is Net Tools from Cre8Labs. One app to switch IP addresses, hand out DHCP, find cameras and keep an eye on a whole site. Let's take a look.
lines.presets-card: Part one. Switch IP in one click.
lines.presets-0: On the left is the adapter you're working on, with its live address, link speed and DNS.
lines.presets-1: To change network, just click a preset. The adapter switches in about a second.
lines.presets-2: Need automatic addressing again? One click puts it back on DHCP. Or press zero.
lines.presets-3: Every preset has its own key. Press two, or click, to jump to the Site A cameras.
lines.presets-4: Let's save a new network as a preset.
lines.presets-7: For the mask, type the full mask, or just slash twenty four.
lines.presets-8: Gateway and DNS are optional, and the subnet is checked as you type.
lines.presets-9: Save it, and the new preset appears on its own tile, with its own shortcut.
lines.presets-10: Shortcuts can be changed, switched off, or set to work from any app.
lines.presets-11: Close the shortcuts window when you're done.
lines.dhcp-card: Part two. A DHCP pool for your cameras.
lines.dhcp-1: Type the network you want to serve. The server address and range are filled in for you.
lines.dhcp-2: Start the pool, plug in your cameras, and watch them pick up addresses.
lines.dhcp-3: To pin a camera to its planned address, add a reservation.
lines.dhcp-4: Name it, so everyone knows which camera it is.
lines.dhcp-5: And set the address it should always get.
lines.dhcp-6: Save, and the camera moves to its reserved address at its next renewal.
lines.dhcp-7: When you're finished, stop the pool, and the adapter goes back to exactly how it was.
lines.scan-card: Part three. Scan and find cameras.
lines.scan-1: Use adapter fills in the network you're plugged into.
lines.scan-2: Press Scan. Each device shows its maker, address, response time and open ports.
lines.scan-3: This camera is still on its factory address. Reach it adds a matching IP, so you can open it straight away.
lines.monitor-card: Part four. Monitor a whole site.
lines.monitor-1: Add everything you just scanned, with one click.
lines.monitor-2: Start monitoring. Every device is pinged once a second, from the adapter you chose.
lines.monitor-3: If a device stops answering, it turns red, and you get an alert straight away.
lines.monitor-4: When it comes back, Net Tools tells you how long it was down.
lines.tools-1: Enter a device to check which ports it has open.
lines.tools-2: Open ports are shown by name. Web, RTSP video, Hikvision SDK and more.
lines.tools-3: To prove a camera is serving video, paste its stream address.
lines.tools-4: Net Tools reads the stream details, like the codec and audio, without playing the video.
lines.tools-5: Traceroute shows the path to any address.
lines.tools-6: Each hop and its response time appear as they're found.
lines.tools-7: And link health shows traffic, errors and dropped packets on the cable.
lines.outro: That's Net Tools. It's free and open source, for Windows ten and eleven. Download it from GitHub, and find more at cre8labs dot U K.
